sequence.assessment: Reduced but unusual US fast-carrier logistics/traffic creates a YELLOW Central-Carolines warning. Smaller raid package makes the strategic cue less obvious than DESECRATE I.
Truk/Ponape approach sectors are prioritized; long-range search/submarine cues raise Truk alert to HIGH without an exact TG fix.

Truk patrol/radar system obtains tactical warning on the approaching strike system. Working first-wave warning is roughly 45-70 minutes, enough for CAP launch/dispersal but not for southern Mobile Fleet intervention.
Carrier positions become attack-quality only intermittently during the raid and expire rapidly on US withdrawal.

new_submarine_sensor_note: Late-April Type 13 air-search radar fitting/trials on new Japanese submarines are a real maturation input for future picket work, but are not treated as an ocean-wide carrier detector or retroactive perfect fix in this event.
system_assessment: The mature Japanese network again succeeds at warning and local readiness, but its persistent mobile-ocean tracking weakness remains. It protects the strategic fleet by preventing a blind sortie rather than by generating a carrier ambush.
